# GoldenCheck Action

> Scan data files for quality problems in CI, post a pull-request comment, and set a pass/fail status check.

## Usage

```yaml
- uses: benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch/packages/actions/goldencheck@main
  with:
    files: "data/*.csv"
```

## Inputs

- `files` -- glob for the data files to scan (required)
- `fail-on` -- severity that fails the job -- `error` (default) or `warning`
- `config` -- path to a goldencheck YAML config
- `llm-boost` -- enable the LLM-enhanced scan (costs money, needs a key)
- `llm-provider` -- which LLM provider to use when boost is on
- `python-version` -- Python to run on
- `version` -- goldencheck version to install

## Outputs

- `errors`, `warnings`, `health-grade`

## Authoritative sources

Read these instead of inferring behaviour from `action.yml`. An input list
gives you names and types; it cannot tell you which defaults are deliberate
or what a knob protects against:

- https://docs.bensevern.dev/docs/goldencheck -- full documentation for the underlying tool.
- `goldencheck/llms.txt` -- ships inside the goldencheck wheel this action installs (`Path(goldencheck.__file__).parent / "llms.txt"`), written for machine readers.
- https://docs.bensevern.dev/docs/llms.txt -- index of every Golden Suite surface.
- https://github.com/benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch -- source, issues, and the decision records.

## Things that are decided, not incidental

- GoldenCheck **discovers rules from the data** rather than requiring you to declare them. With no config it profiles the file and reports what looks wrong; a config pins expectations so drift fails the build.
- `llm-boost` is off by default and stays off unless you both set it and supply a key. The default scan is deterministic, offline and free.
- `health-grade` is an A-F letter, and it is the WORST grade across all matched files, not an average. It is a summary for humans -- gate on `fail-on` and the error count, not on the letter.
